hi.Pour cream mixture evenly over the layer: क्रीम मिश्रण परतों पर समान रूप से डालें। फ़ॉइल से कसकर ढकें और 30 मिनट बेक करें ताकि चाकू कद्दू में केवल हल्के प्रतिरोध से जाए।
hi.Mix breadcrumbs with remaining cheese an: ब्रेडक्रम्ब, बचा चीज़ और 10 ग्राम पिघला मक्खन मिलाएँ। फ़ॉइल हटाकर ऊपर छिड़कें और 15–20 मिनट गहरा सुनहरा तथा कद्दू पूरी तरह नरम होने तक बेक करें। काटने से पहले 10 मिनट रखें।
hi.Slice squash thinly and evenly so the ce: स्क्वैश समान मोटाई में पतला काटें ताकि चीज़ भूरा होने से पहले बीच तक पक जाए; स्पष्ट शाकाहारी लिखा चीज़ चुनें।

gu.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: માત્રા ચાર પુખ્ત વ્યક્તિઓ માટે છે. દરેક પગલામાં પાકવાના સંકેત તપાસો અને સ્વાદ પ્રમાણે મસાલો ગોઠવો. જૈન યોગ્યતા તમારા પરિવારના સામગ્રીના નિયમો પર આધારિત છે.
gu.butternut squash, peeled and thinly slic: બટરનટ કોળું, છાલ ઉતારી પાતળું સમારેલું
gu.vegetarian Gruyère-style cheese, grated: વેજિટેરિયન રેનેટવાળું ગ્રુયેર જેવું ચીઝ, છીણેલું
gu.Heat oven to 190°C. Peel and seed squash: ઓવન 190°C પર ગરમ કરો. કોળાની છાલ અને બી કાઢી સરખી 3 મિમી કતરીઓ કરો. છીછરી બેકિંગ ડિશમાં 15 ગ્રામ માખણ લગાવો.
gu.Melt 10 g butter in a pan and cook onion: પૅનમાં 10 ગ્રામ માખણ ઓગાળી ડુંગળી 7 મિનિટ નરમ કરો; લસણ અને થાઇમ 1 મિનિટ હલાવો. ક્રીમ, દૂધ, મીઠું, મરી અને જાયફળ ફેંટો.
gu.Layer half the squash in the dish, overl: અડધાં કોળાની કતરીઓ એકબીજા ઉપર ચડાવી ડિશમાં ગોઠવો. અડધી ડુંગળી અને ત્રીજા ભાગનું ચીઝ છાંટો; બાકીનાં કોળા અને ડુંગળીથી પડ ફરી ગોઠવો.
gu.Pour cream mixture evenly over the layer: ક્રીમનું મિશ્રણ પડ પર સરખું રેડો. ફોઇલથી બરાબર ઢાંકી 30 મિનિટ બેક કરો જેથી કોળામાં ચપ્પુ માત્ર થોડા પ્રતિકારથી જાય.
gu.Mix breadcrumbs with remaining cheese an: બ્રેડક્રમ્બ, બાકીનું ચીઝ અને 10 ગ્રામ ઓગળેલું માખણ ભેળવો. ફોઇલ હટાવી ઉપર છાંટી 15–20 મિનિટ ઘેરું સોનેરી અને કોળું સંપૂર્ણ નરમ થાય ત્યાં સુધી બેક કરો. કાપતાં પહેલાં 10 મિનિટ રાખો.
gu.Slice squash thinly and evenly so the ce: સ્ક્વોશને સરખી જાડાઈમાં પાતળું કાપો જેથી ચીઝ ભૂખરું થાય પહેલાં વચ્ચે સુધી પાકે; સ્પષ્ટ શાકાહારી લખેલું ચીઝ પસંદ કરો.

recipe.name: Paneer Do Pyaza
steps: Separate 300 g onion into large petals and finely chop the other 250 g. Heat 15 ml oil in a pan and sear onion petals over high heat for 3–4 minutes so their edges colour but centres stay crisp; remove.
Add remaining oil and butter to the pan. Crackle cumin, add chopped onion and cook 8 minutes until golden. Stir in ginger-garlic paste and green chilies for 1 minute.
Add coriander, turmeric and chilli powder for 30 seconds, then tomato purée and 7 g salt. Cook uncovered for 8–10 minutes until thick and oil appears at the edges.
Lower heat and whisk yogurt into the masala a spoonful at a time. Add 180 ml water, paneer cubes and seared onion petals; simmer gently for 5 minutes without breaking the paneer.
Sprinkle garam masala, crushed dried fenugreek and remaining 3 g salt. Rest 5 minutes and serve with naan or roti. The second addition of onion petals is what makes this do pyaza distinct.
tips: Keep the later-added onion petals slightly crisp and simmer paneer only briefly; this preserves the dish's two onion textures and soft cheese.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: मात्राएँ चार वयस्कों के लिए हैं। हर चरण में पकने के संकेत जाँचें और स्वाद के अनुसार मसाला बदलें। जैन उपयुक्तता आपके परिवार की सामग्री संबंधी नियमों पर निर्भर है।
hi.Separate 300 g onion into large petals a: 300 ग्राम प्याज़ को बड़ी पंखुड़ियों में अलग करें और बाकी 250 ग्राम बारीक काटें। पैन में 15 मिली तेल गरम कर बड़ी पंखुड़ियाँ तेज़ आँच पर 3–4 मिनट किनारे रंगने पर पर बीच से कुरकुरी रहने तक सेकें और निकालें।
पैन में बचा तेल और मक्खन डालें। जीरा चटकाकर बारीक प्याज़ 8 मिनट सुनहरा पकाएँ। अदरक-लहसुन पेस्ट और हरी मिर्च 1 मिनट चलाएँ।
hi.Add coriander, turmeric and chilli powde: धनिया, हल्दी और मिर्च पाउडर 30 सेकंड चलाएँ, फिर टमाटर प्यूरी और 7 ग्राम नमक डालें। 8–10 मिनट बिना ढके गाढ़ा और किनारों पर तेल दिखने तक पकाएँ।
hi.Lower heat and whisk yogurt into the mas: आँच धीमी कर दही एक-एक चम्मच फेंटकर मसाले में डालें। 180 मिली पानी, पनीर के टुकड़े और सिकी प्याज़ पंखुड़ियाँ मिलाएँ; पनीर तोड़े बिना 5 मिनट हल्का उबालें।
hi.Sprinkle garam masala, crushed dried fen: गरम मसाला, मसलकर कसूरी मेथी और बचा 3 ग्राम नमक डालें। 5 मिनट रखकर नान या रोटी के साथ परोसें। प्याज़ की दूसरी बार डाली गई पंखुड़ियाँ ही इसे दो प्याज़ा बनाती हैं।
hi.Keep the later-added onion petals slight: बाद में डाली प्याज़ पंखुड़ियाँ थोड़ी कुरकुरी रखें और पनीर कम देर उबालें; इससे दो तरह का प्याज़ और नरम पनीर बने रहते हैं।

gu.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: માત્રા ચાર પુખ્ત વ્યક્તિઓ માટે છે. દરેક પગલામાં પાકવાના સંકેત તપાસો અને સ્વાદ પ્રમાણે મસાલો ગોઠવો. જૈન યોગ્યતા તમારા પરિવારના સામગ્રીના નિયમો પર આધારિત છે.
gu.Separate 300 g onion into large petals a: 300 ગ્રામ ડુંગળીને મોટા પડમાં છૂટી કરો અને બાકીની 250 ગ્રામ બારીક સમારો. પૅનમાં 15 મિલી તેલ ગરમ કરી મોટા પડ ઊંચા તાપે 3–4 મિનિટ કિનારી રંગાય પણ વચ્ચે કરકરા રહે ત્યાં સુધી શેકી કાઢો.
પૅનમાં બાકીનું તેલ અને માખણ નાખો. જીરું તતડાવી બારીક ડુંગળી 8 મિનિટ સોનેરી કરો. આદુ-લસણની પેસ્ટ અને લીલાં મરચાં 1 મિનિટ હલાવો.
gu.Add coriander, turmeric and chilli powde: ધાણા, હળદર અને મરચું પાઉડર 30 સેકન્ડ હલાવો, પછી ટામેટાંની પ્યુરી અને 7 ગ્રામ મીઠું નાખો. 8–10 મિનિટ ઢાંક્યા વગર ઘાટું અને કિનારીથી તેલ છૂટે ત્યાં સુધી રાંધો.
gu.Lower heat and whisk yogurt into the mas: તાપ ધીમો કરી દહીં એક-એક ચમચી ફેંટીને મસાલામાં નાખો. 180 મિલી પાણી, પનીરના ટુકડા અને શેકેલી ડુંગળીના પડ ભેળવો; પનીર તૂટે નહીં તેમ 5 મિનિટ હળવેથી ઉકાળો.
gu.Sprinkle garam masala, crushed dried fen: ગરમ મસાલો, મસળેલી કસૂરી મેથી અને બાકીનું 3 ગ્રામ મીઠું નાખો. 5 મિનિટ રાખી નાન કે રોટલી સાથે પીરસો. બીજી વખત ઉમેરેલા ડુંગળીના પડ જ તેને દો પ્યાઝા બનાવે છે.
gu.Keep the later-added onion petals slight: પછી ઉમેરેલી ડુંગળીના પડ સહેજ કરકરા રાખો અને પનીર થોડો સમય જ ઉકાળો; તેથી બે પ્રકારની ડુંગળી અને નરમ પનીર રહે છે.

recipe.name: Paneer Handi
steps: Soak cashews in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend with 80 ml of the measured water until smooth. Cube and cover the paneer so it does not dry out.
Heat ghee in a heavy pan on medium heat. Cook onion for 8–10 minutes until golden; add ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 minute until its raw smell disappears.
Add tomato puree, chili powder, coriander powder and salt. Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until the puree darkens and ghee separates at the edges.
Stir in cashew paste and remaining 170 ml water. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until gravy coats a spoon. Lower the heat before adding cream and garam masala.
Fold in paneer and warm for 3–4 minutes without a hard boil so the cubes remain tender. Taste for salt, top with coriander and serve with roti.
tips: A heavy pan works if you do not have a clay handi; avoid boiling paneer after adding it.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: मात्राएँ चार वयस्कों के लिए हैं। हर चरण में पकने के संकेत जाँचें और स्वाद के अनुसार मसाला बदलें। जैन उपयुक्तता आपके परिवार की सामग्री संबंधी नियमों पर निर्भर है।
hi.Soak cashews in hot water for 15 minutes: काजू 15 मिनट गरम पानी में भिगोएँ, फिर दिए गए पानी में से 80 मि.ली. लेकर चिकना पीसें। पनीर काटकर ढक दें ताकि सूखे नहीं।
भारी पैन में घी मध्यम आँच पर गरम करें। प्याज़ 8–10 मिनट सुनहरा करें; अदरक-लहसुन पेस्ट डालकर कच्ची गंध जाने तक 1 मिनट चलाएँ।
hi.Add tomato puree, chili powder, coriande: टमाटर प्यूरी, मिर्च, धनिया पाउडर और नमक डालें। 8–10 मिनट बार-बार चलाते हुए पकाएँ, जब तक प्यूरी गहरी हो और किनारों पर घी अलग दिखे।
hi.Stir in cashew paste and remaining 170 m: काजू पेस्ट और बचा 170 मि.ली. पानी मिलाएँ। 5 मिनट हल्का उबालें, जब तक ग्रेवी चम्मच पर टिके। क्रीम और गरम मसाला डालने से पहले आँच धीमी करें।
hi.Fold in paneer and warm for 3–4 minutes: पनीर धीरे मिलाकर तेज़ उबाल के बिना 3–4 मिनट गरम करें ताकि टुकड़े नरम रहें। नमक जाँचें, हरा धनिया डालें और रोटी के साथ परोसें।
hi.A heavy pan works if you do not have a c: मिट्टी की हांडी न हो तो भारी पैन लें; पनीर डालने के बाद तेज़ उबाल न आने दें।

gu.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: માત્રા ચાર પુખ્ત વ્યક્તિઓ માટે છે. દરેક પગલામાં પાકવાના સંકેત તપાસો અને સ્વાદ પ્રમાણે મસાલો ગોઠવો. જૈન યોગ્યતા તમારા પરિવારના સામગ્રીના નિયમો પર આધારિત છે.
gu.Soak cashews in hot water for 15 minutes: કાજુ 15 મિનિટ ગરમ પાણીમાં પલાળો, પછી આપેલા પાણીમાંથી 80 મિ.લી. લઈ મસૃણ પીસો. પનીર કાપી ઢાંકી રાખો જેથી સુકાય નહીં.
ભારે કડાઈમાં ઘી મધ્યમ તાપે ગરમ કરો. ડુંગળી 8–10 મિનિટ સોનેરી કરો; આદુ-લસણની પેસ્ટ નાખી કાચી સુગંધ જાય ત્યાં સુધી 1 મિનિટ હલાવો.
gu.Add tomato puree, chili powder, coriande: ટામેટાની પ્યુરી, મરચું, ધાણા પાઉડર અને મીઠું નાખો. 8–10 મિનિટ વારંવાર હલાવી પ્યુરી ઘેરી થાય અને કિનારે ઘી છૂટે ત્યાં સુધી રાંધો.
gu.Stir in cashew paste and remaining 170 m: કાજુની પેસ્ટ અને બાકીનું 170 મિ.લી. પાણી ઉમેરો. ગ્રેવી ચમચીને ચોંટે ત્યાં સુધી 5 મિનિટ ધીમે ઉકાળો. ક્રીમ અને ગરમ મસાલો ઉમેરતા પહેલાં તાપ ધીમો કરો.
gu.Fold in paneer and warm for 3–4 minutes: પનીર હળવેથી ભેળવી જોરદાર ઉકાળો ટાળી 3–4 મિનિટ ગરમ કરો જેથી ટુકડા નરમ રહે. મીઠું ચાખો, કોથમીર ભભરાવી રોટલી સાથે પીરસો.
gu.A heavy pan works if you do not have a c: માટીની હાંડી ન હોય તો ભારે કડાઈ લો; પનીર ઉમેર્યા પછી જોરદાર ઉકાળો ટાળો.

recipe.name: Paneer Jalfrezi
steps: Cut paneer and vegetables into similar-length strips. Pat paneer dry, and keep peppers separate from tomato so they stay crisp.
Heat half the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Sear paneer for 1 minute per side until lightly golden; lift it out before it toughens.
Add remaining oil and cumin to the pan. Stir-fry onion and peppers for 4–5 minutes so their edges char slightly while the centers remain firm.
Add ginger, garlic, chopped tomato, tomato paste, coriander powder, chili powder and salt. Cook 4–5 minutes until tomato becomes a thick coating, not watery gravy.
Return paneer, toss gently for 2 minutes to coat, and turn off heat. Add lemon juice and coriander; serve immediately with roti.
tips: Jalfrezi should be semi-dry with distinct crisp pepper and paneer strips, not a smooth curry.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Heat half the oil in a wide pan over med: चौड़े पैन में आधा तेल मध्यम-तेज़ आँच पर गरम करें। पनीर हर तरफ़ 1 मिनट हल्का सुनहरा सेंककर सख्त होने से पहले निकालें।
बचा तेल और जीरा डालें। प्याज़ और शिमला मिर्च 4–5 मिनट तेज़ी से भूनें, किनारे थोड़े झुलसें लेकिन बीच में कसावट रहे।

recipe.name: Paneer Hariyali
steps: Blanch spinach in boiling water for 1 minute and cool immediately in cold water; squeeze gently. Blend spinach, coriander, mint, green chili, cashews and 80 ml water to a smooth green puree.
Heat oil in a heavy pan on medium heat. Add cumin and onion; cook 7–8 minutes until onion softens and turns pale golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
Lower heat. Add the green puree and remaining 100 ml water; simmer 4 minutes, stirring, until the raw herb taste mellows but the color stays bright.
Whisk yogurt smooth with a spoonful of warm gravy. Stir it slowly into the pan, then add salt and garam masala. Keep heat low and do not boil vigorously.
Add paneer cubes and heat gently for 3 minutes, just until warm through. Turn off heat, stir in lemon juice, and serve with phulka or rice.
tips: Blanching and rapid cooling keep the herb gravy green; overheating the yogurt can split it.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

hi.Quantities serve four adults. Check the: मात्राएँ चार वयस्कों के लिए हैं। हर चरण में पकने के संकेत जाँचें और स्वाद के अनुसार मसाला बदलें। जैन उपयुक्तता आपके परिवार की सामग्री संबंधी नियमों पर निर्भर है।
hi.Blanch spinach in boiling water for 1 mi: पालक 1 मिनट उबलते पानी में डालकर तुरंत ठंडे पानी में ठंडा करें और हल्का निचोड़ें। पालक, धनिया, पुदीना, हरी मिर्च, काजू और 80 मि.ली. पानी चिकना हरा पीसें।
भारी पैन में तेल मध्यम आँच पर गरम करें। जीरा और प्याज़ डालकर 7–8 मिनट नरम और हल्का सुनहरा करें। अदरक-लहसुन पेस्ट डालकर 1 मिनट पकाएँ।
hi.Lower heat. Add the green puree and rema: आँच धीमी करें। हरी प्यूरी और बचा 100 मि.ली. पानी डालकर 4 मिनट चलाते हुए पकाएँ, ताकि कच्चा स्वाद जाए लेकिन रंग चमकीला रहे।

hi.Add paneer cubes and heat gently for 3 m: पनीर डालकर सिर्फ गरम होने तक 3 मिनट धीरे पकाएँ। आँच बंद करें, नींबू रस मिलाएँ और फुल्के या चावल के साथ परोसें।
hi.Blanching and rapid cooling keep the her: पालक को तुरंत ठंडा करने से ग्रेवी हरी रहती है; दही तेज़ उबालने पर फट सकता है।

recipe.name: Paneer Ghee Roast
steps: Whisk yogurt with 3 g salt and coat paneer cubes. Set aside for 15 minutes while preparing the roast masala.
Dry-roast chilies, coriander, cumin, fennel, pepper and fenugreek on low heat for 3–4 minutes until fragrant, without burning. Cool, then blend with tamarind and 100 ml water into a thick paste.
Heat half the ghee in a wide pan. Sear marinated paneer on two sides for about 2 minutes total and remove; keep the heat moderate so the yogurt does not scorch.
Add remaining ghee, curry leaves and spice paste. Stir frequently for 8–10 minutes until the paste deepens to brick-red and ghee appears at the edges; add jaggery and remaining salt.
Fold paneer into the thick masala and cook 2–3 minutes until every cube is coated. Serve warm with neer dosa or rice; this roast should be thick, not soupy.
tips: Mild Kashmiri chilies give the traditional deep red color without relying on food dye.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Paneer Chettinad
steps: Dry-roast coriander seeds, pepper, fennel, cumin, red chilies and cinnamon on low heat for 3–4 minutes until fragrant. Add coconut for the last minute, cool, and grind with 100 ml water into a coarse paste.
Heat oil in a pan. Fry curry leaves for 20 seconds, then add onion and cook 7–8 minutes until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add tomato and salt; cook 6–8 minutes until soft and thick. Stir in the roasted spice-coconut paste and cook 3 minutes, scraping the bottom so it does not stick.
Pour in remaining 180 ml water and simmer 6 minutes until the gravy is aromatic and lightly thickened. Taste and adjust salt, keeping the pepper flavor prominent.
Add paneer cubes and warm gently for 3 minutes without a fierce boil. Serve hot with rice, appam or chapati.
tips: Freshly roasted whole spices and coconut define this Chettinad masala; keep the paneer tender.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Dahi Kofta
steps: Mix crumbled paneer, mashed potato, chickpea flour, half the ginger, 4 g salt and half the coriander leaves. Knead just until the mixture holds, then shape 12 firm balls.
Heat 70 ml oil in a small deep pan. Fry kofta in batches on medium heat for 4–5 minutes, turning, until evenly golden. Drain on paper; do not crowd the pan.

Whisk yogurt with 250 ml water until smooth. Heat remaining oil in a wide pan; add cumin and onion, cooking 6 minutes until golden. Stir in remaining ginger, coriander powder, turmeric and chili for 1 minute.
Reduce heat to low and slowly stir in the yogurt. Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring constantly at first, until lightly thickened; keep below a hard boil to prevent splitting. Season with remaining salt.
Set the hot kofta in a serving dish and spoon warm yogurt gravy over them just before eating. Sprinkle the remaining coriander; serve with rice or chapati.
tips: Keep kofta separate until serving so they retain their golden exterior.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Cabbage Kofta
steps: Toss shredded cabbage with 4 g salt and leave 10 minutes. Squeeze firmly to remove excess water; this keeps kofta from falling apart.
Mix squeezed cabbage with chickpea flour, half the green chili and half the coriander leaves. Shape 12 compact balls; add a spoon of squeezed cabbage liquid only if the mixture is too dry.
Heat 75 ml oil in a deep pan. Fry the kofta in batches over medium heat for 5–6 minutes until cooked through and golden; drain well.

Heat remaining oil in a separate pan. Add cumin and onion, cooking 7 minutes until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste, remaining chili, tomato puree, coriander powder, turmeric and remaining salt; cook 8 minutes until thick.
Add 220 ml water and simmer gravy for 5 minutes. Place kofta in the serving bowl, ladle gravy over just before serving, and garnish with coriander.
tips: Finely shred and squeeze cabbage; wet cabbage makes the kofta oil-heavy and fragile.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Soya Kofta Curry
steps: Soak soya granules in boiling water for 10 minutes, drain and squeeze very dry. Chop finely; blend cashews with 80 ml of the measured water until smooth.
Mix squeezed soya with mashed potato, chickpea flour, 4 g salt and half the coriander leaves. Shape 12 compact kofta balls; chill 10 minutes so they hold together.
Heat 75 ml oil in a deep pan. Fry kofta in batches on medium heat for 5–6 minutes until deep golden; drain on paper.

In a separate pan, heat remaining oil and cook onion 7 minutes. Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, coriander powder, chili and remaining salt; cook 8 minutes until thick. Stir in cashew paste and remaining 220 ml water.
Simmer gravy 5 minutes, then add garam masala. Put kofta in the serving bowl and spoon gravy over them just before eating; garnish with remaining coriander.
tips: Squeezing soaked soya thoroughly prevents spongy, fragile kofta.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Nizami Handi
steps: Soak cashews 15 minutes in hot water, then blend smooth with 100 ml measured water. Steep saffron in 20 ml warm water. Cut all vegetables to similar size.
Blanch cauliflower, carrot, peas and beans in boiling water for 4 minutes. Add spinach for the final minute, then drain everything; vegetables should stay firm because they cook again in sauce.
Heat ghee in a handi. Cook sliced onion 8 minutes until light golden; add ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute. Stir in tomato puree, coriander powder and garam masala; cook 6 minutes until thick.

Lower heat. Stir in cashew paste and remaining 180 ml water, then whisked yogurt one spoon at a time so the tomato-cashew sauce stays smooth. Add blanched vegetables, spinach and salt; simmer gently 6 minutes.
Add paneer, cream and saffron water. Warm 3 minutes without a hard boil, taste for seasoning and serve in the handi with naan or rice.
tips: A tomato-cashew base, spinach and mixed vegetables distinguish Nizami Handi; keep the yogurt simmer gentle.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Makhana Curry
steps: Roast makhana in 10 g ghee over low-medium heat for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until crisp and lightly golden. Remove promptly so they do not burn.
Soak cashews in hot water 15 minutes and blend with 80 ml measured water until smooth. Heat remaining ghee and cook onion for 7 minutes until golden; add ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add tomato puree, coriander powder, chili and salt. Cook 8–10 minutes until thick and the ghee separates at the edges.
Stir in cashew paste and remaining 220 ml water. Simmer 5 minutes, then add cream and garam masala on low heat.
Fold roasted makhana into the hot gravy and simmer only 2 minutes so the centers soften but retain shape. Sprinkle coriander and serve at once with roti.
tips: Add roasted makhana shortly before serving; long soaking makes them mushy.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Matar Mushroom
steps: Wipe mushrooms clean and halve them; do not soak them in water. Boil peas for 3–4 minutes until almost tender and drain.
Heat oil in a wide pan, add cumin and onion, and cook 7 minutes until golden. Stir in ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add tomato, coriander powder, turmeric, chili and salt. Cook 7–8 minutes until tomato breaks down and oil shows at the edges.
Add mushrooms and stir-fry 5 minutes until their released moisture mostly evaporates. Add peas and 150 ml water; simmer 5 minutes until both are tender.
Taste and adjust salt, then scatter coriander leaves. Serve this semi-dry curry hot with chapati or rice.
tips: Brown mushrooms before adding water for a fuller flavor.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Kadai Mushroom
steps: Dry-roast coriander seeds, red chilies, cumin and pepper for 2 minutes on low heat. Cool and crush coarsely to make fresh kadai masala.
Wipe mushrooms clean. Heat half the oil in a kadai and sauté mushrooms 5–6 minutes until their water evaporates and edges brown; remove.
Add remaining oil and cook onion 5 minutes. Add ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then tomato puree and salt; cook 7 minutes until thick and glossy.
Add both peppers and stir-fry 4 minutes so they remain firm. Add crushed kadai masala and 120 ml water; simmer 3 minutes.
Return mushrooms and warm 2 minutes. Crush dried fenugreek over the top and serve hot with roti.
tips: Fresh coarse kadai masala and peppers distinguish this from ordinary mushroom curry.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Mushroom Chettinad
steps: Dry-roast peppercorns, fennel, coriander seeds and chilies on low heat for 2–3 minutes. Add coconut for the final minute; cool and grind with 70 ml water to a coarse paste.
Wipe mushrooms dry and halve. Heat oil in a wide pan; sauté mushrooms 5 minutes until their moisture evaporates, then remove.
In the same pan, fry curry leaves 20 seconds and onion 6 minutes until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and stir 1 minute; add tomato and salt and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in coarse spice-coconut paste and remaining 80 ml water. Cook 5 minutes, stirring, until dark and aromatic; return mushrooms and toss well.
Simmer 3 minutes until mushrooms are coated in the thick peppery masala. Serve hot with rice or chapati.
tips: Black pepper and roasted coconut should lead the flavor; avoid making it a generic tomato gravy.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Baby Corn Masala
steps: Blanch halved baby corn in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain. Soak cashews in hot water 10 minutes and blend with 70 ml measured water until smooth.
Heat oil in a wide pan. Add cumin and onion; cook 6–7 minutes until golden. Stir in ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add tomato puree, coriander powder, chili and salt. Cook 7–8 minutes until thick and glossy. Stir in cashew paste and remaining 130 ml water.
Add baby corn and bell pepper. Cover and simmer 6 minutes until corn is tender but still slightly crisp and the pepper remains bright.
Add garam masala, taste salt, and simmer uncovered 2 minutes if the gravy is thin. Garnish with coriander and serve with roti.
tips: Use tender baby corn and avoid overcooking so its characteristic crunch remains.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Afghani Soya Chaap
steps: Soak cashews in hot water for 15 minutes and blend with green chili to a fine paste. Cut soya chaap into thick pieces, pat dry and score lightly so the marinade enters.
Whisk yogurt, cashew paste, cream, ginger-garlic, lemon juice, white pepper, garam masala and salt. Coat chaap thoroughly and refrigerate 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Thread chaap onto skewers or spread on a lined tray, leaving space between pieces. Brush lightly with oil.
Roast 15–18 minutes, turning once, until hot through with charred spots at the edges. For a skillet, sear on medium-high heat 4–5 minutes per side.
Rest 3 minutes, sprinkle coriander, and serve hot with lemon and mint chutney. Do not bury the charred chaap in extra sauce.
tips: Choose clearly labelled vegetarian soya chaap and check the package ingredients before marinating.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Soya Keema Matar
steps: Cover soya granules with boiling water for 10 minutes, drain and squeeze very dry. Fluff with a fork to keep a mince-like texture.
Heat oil in a wide pan. Add cumin and onion; cook 7–8 minutes until golden. Stir in ginger-garlic and green chili for 1 minute.
Add tomato, coriander powder, turmeric and salt. Cook 8 minutes, stirring, until the tomato is thick and oil appears at the edges.
Add squeezed soya and peas; stir-fry 3 minutes to coat each granule. Add 180 ml water, cover and simmer 8 minutes until peas are tender and the mixture remains moist, not soupy.
Stir in garam masala and simmer uncovered 2 minutes. Scatter coriander leaves and serve with roti or eggless pav.
tips: Use small soya granules rather than whole chunks for a proper keema texture.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Tofu Tikka Masala
steps: Press tofu for 20 minutes and cut into 2 cm cubes. Whisk yogurt with half the ginger-garlic, half the chili, 3 g garam masala, lemon juice and 4 g salt; coat tofu and marinate 20 minutes.
Spread tofu on a lined tray, brush with 15 ml oil and roast at 220°C for 18–20 minutes, turning once, until the edges char lightly.

Meanwhile heat remaining oil in a pan. Cook onion 8 minutes until golden; add remaining ginger-garlic for 1 minute. Stir in tomato puree, coriander powder, remaining chili and salt; cook 9 minutes until thick.
Add 180 ml water and simmer sauce for 5 minutes. Lower the heat, stir in cream and remaining garam masala, and keep just below a boil.
Fold roasted tofu into the sauce and warm 2 minutes, preserving the charred edges. Sprinkle coriander and serve with rice or roti.
tips: For a dairy-free version, use unsweetened plant yogurt and coconut cream in the same quantities.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Ruwangan Chaman
steps: Pat paneer slices dry. Heat mustard oil until it just begins to smoke, lower the heat, and shallow-fry paneer 2–3 minutes per side until golden; remove carefully.
In the same oil add cinnamon and crushed cardamom for 30 seconds. Add tomato puree and cook 6 minutes until its raw smell fades and the sauce thickens.

Pour in remaining 200 ml water, cover and simmer 10 minutes until the red tomato gravy coats a spoon. Return paneer and simmer gently 4 minutes.
Crush black cumin and dried mint over the curry. Rest covered for 10 minutes so the paneer absorbs the Kashmiri sauce, then serve warm with rice.
tips: This Kashmiri tomato-paneer dish uses dry ginger and fennel, not a creamy onion-cashew base.

recipe.name: Al Yakhni

ingredients.name: bottle gourd, peeled and thick wedges

steps: Peel bottle gourd, remove hard seeds if present and cut into thick wedges. Whisk yogurt very smooth with 120 ml measured water, fennel powder and dry ginger.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy pan until lightly smoking, then reduce to medium. Shallow-fry gourd in batches for 6–8 minutes until edges are golden and centers nearly tender; remove.
In the remaining oil bloom cumin, cardamom, cinnamon and asafoetida for 30 seconds. Add remaining 100 ml water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Turn heat very low. Pour in whisked yogurt slowly, stirring continuously for 5–6 minutes until hot and slightly thickened; do not let it boil hard or separate. Add salt.
Return gourd, cover and simmer very gently 8–10 minutes until fully tender. Serve the pale fennel-scented yakhni with steamed rice.
tips: Use full-fat room-temperature yogurt and low heat to prevent curdling; this curry has no tomato.

recipe.name: Gucchi Matar
steps: Soak dried morels in 300 ml warm water for 20 minutes. Lift out, split large caps and rinse carefully to remove grit; strain and reserve the soaking liquid.
Heat ghee in a heavy pan. Cook onion 7 minutes until golden, then add ginger for 1 minute. Add tomato puree, coriander powder, chili and salt; cook 8 minutes until thick.
Whisk yogurt with a spoonful of warm masala, lower the heat and stir it into the pan. Add cleaned morels and 200 ml strained soaking liquid; cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Add peas and simmer 7–8 minutes until peas are tender and morels are soft but still springy. Add a little remaining soaking liquid if gravy becomes too thick.
Stir in garam masala, taste the salt and finish with coriander leaves. Serve warm with basmati rice so the morel aroma remains prominent.
tips: Gucchi are true honeycomb morels, not ordinary button mushrooms; wash away every grain of grit.

recipe.name: Rajasthani Haldi ki Sabzi

ingredients.name: fresh turmeric root, peeled and grated

steps: Wear gloves to peel and grate fresh turmeric finely. Boil peas 3 minutes and drain; whisk yogurt smooth with 120 ml water.
Heat ghee on medium-low heat. Add cumin, then grated turmeric and ginger; cook 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until the raw sharpness softens and turmeric turns golden.
Add green chili, coriander powder, red chili powder and salt. Stir 1 minute, then add peas and cook 3 minutes to coat them with spiced turmeric.
Turn heat low. Add whisked yogurt gradually, stirring continuously, and simmer gently 5 minutes without a hard boil so it does not split.
Taste for salt, garnish with coriander and serve warm in small portions with bajra roti or chapati.
tips: This winter dish uses fresh turmeric root, not a large quantity of dried turmeric powder.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Sev ki Sabzi
steps: Choose thick sev that will hold its shape in hot gravy. Chop tomatoes finely and keep the sev dry until the moment of serving.
Heat oil in a pan; add mustard and cumin and let them crackle for 30 seconds. Add chopped tomato, turmeric, chili, coriander powder and salt.
Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until tomatoes break down to a glossy thick sauce. Add jaggery and stir until dissolved.
Add 250 ml water and simmer 4 minutes. Taste for a balanced sweet-tangy-spicy flavor; adjust salt if needed.
Turn off heat. Fold in half the sev briefly, ladle into bowls, then top with remaining crisp sev and coriander. Serve immediately with rotli.
tips: Use thick sev, not fine chaat sev; add it at serving time to avoid a soggy curry.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Shev Bhaji
steps: Dry-roast coconut and half the onion over low heat for 5–6 minutes until brown and nutty. Cool and grind with garlic and ginger to a thick paste.
Heat oil in a pan. Cook remaining onion for 6 minutes until golden. Stir in the coconut paste and roast 4 minutes, scraping the bottom.
Add tomato, kala masala, chili powder and salt; cook 5 minutes until the masala darkens and oil shows at the edges.
Pour in 450 ml water and simmer uncovered 8 minutes to make a spicy, pourable rassa. Taste the salt before adding shev.
Add half the thick shev just before serving, ladle curry into bowls and top with remaining shev and coriander. Serve with jowar bhakri while some shev stays crisp.
tips: This Maharashtrian onion-coconut rassa is distinct from Gujarati tomato-based sev sabzi.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Kaju Usal
steps: If using dry raw cashews, soak them in hot water for 30 minutes and drain; fresh tender cashews need no soaking. Grind coconut with 100 ml measured water to a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a heavy pan. Crackle mustard seeds and curry leaves for 30 seconds, then cook onion 7 minutes until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add tomato, goda masala, chili, turmeric and salt. Cook 6 minutes until thick; add coconut paste and cook another 3 minutes, stirring.
Add cashews and remaining 250 ml water. Cover and simmer 10–12 minutes until cashews are tender but intact and the coconut gravy coats them.
Taste the seasoning and simmer uncovered briefly if too thin. Garnish with coriander and serve hot with chapati or rice.
tips: Fresh tender cashews are traditional; soaked raw cashews are a practical substitute.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Goan Vegetable Vindaloo
steps: Soak dried chilies in hot water for 10 minutes. Grind them with garlic, ginger, vinegar, cumin, pepper and cinnamon into a smooth red vindaloo paste.
Heat oil in a heavy pot. Cook onion 7 minutes until golden; add vindaloo paste and fry 4–5 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and the raw vinegar edge softens.
Add potato and carrot, toss in paste for 2 minutes, then add 350 ml water and salt. Cover and simmer 10 minutes until almost tender.
Add cauliflower and pepper; simmer uncovered 8–10 minutes until vegetables are cooked but not mushy and sauce is deep red and tangy.
Rest covered 10 minutes for the vinegar and spice flavors to settle. Taste salt and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Vinegar, dried chilies and garlic define vindaloo; do not replace the tang with only tomato.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Goan Vegetable Caldine
steps: Cut vegetables to similar size. Lightly toast coriander and cumin for 2 minutes, then grind them finely with turmeric and 100 ml coconut milk to make the mild caldine spice mix.
Heat coconut oil in a heavy pot. Cook onion 5 minutes until translucent, not brown; add ginger, garlic and slit green chili and stir for 1 minute.
Add potato, carrot, beans and cauliflower; stir in spice mix, 200 ml water and salt. Cover and simmer 8 minutes until vegetables are almost tender.
Add peas and remaining 400 ml coconut milk. Simmer gently 5–6 minutes until everything is just cooked; avoid a vigorous boil that can split the milk.
Turn off heat, stir in lemon juice and taste salt. Serve this pale golden, mildly spiced coconut curry with steamed rice.
tips: Caldine is a mild yellow coconut curry; keep red chili and deep roasting out of it.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Vegetable Ghassi
steps: Dry-roast chilies, coriander and cumin for 3 minutes until fragrant. Add half the coconut for the last minute; cool and grind with tamarind and 150 ml measured water to a smooth red paste.
Heat coconut oil in a heavy pot. Crackle mustard seeds and curry leaves for 30 seconds. Add potatoes and carrots and toss for 2 minutes.
Add 250 ml remaining water and salt, cover and cook 7 minutes. Add beans and cauliflower; cook 5 minutes until all vegetables are almost tender.
Stir in red coconut-spice paste and jaggery. Simmer uncovered 7–8 minutes until gravy thickens and coats the vegetables; add the remaining fresh coconut.
Taste for sweet-sour-spicy balance and salt. Serve hot with neer dosa or rice.
tips: Roasted chilies, coconut and tamarind give ghassi its signature deep red coastal gravy.

recipe.name: Menaskai
steps: Toast sesame seeds on low heat until fragrant and set aside. Dry-roast red chilies and coconut for 2–3 minutes until the coconut is lightly golden; cool.
Grind roasted sesame, coconut and chilies with tamarind and 100 ml measured water into a smooth thick paste.
Put pineapple, jaggery, turmeric, salt and remaining 180 ml water in a pan. Simmer 8 minutes until pineapple softens and releases its juice.
Stir in coconut-sesame paste and simmer 6–8 minutes until glossy, thick and sweet-sour-spicy. Stir often to prevent the jaggery from catching.
Heat coconut oil in a small pan and crackle mustard seeds and curry leaves. Pour tempering over the menaskai; rest 5 minutes and serve with rice.
tips: Menaskai is a thick pineapple, sesame and coconut relish-curry, not a thin sweet soup.

recipe.name: Vegetable Moilee
steps: Cut vegetables to similar bite-sized pieces. Heat coconut oil in a deep pan and cook sliced onion 5 minutes until soft and translucent, not browned.
Add ginger, slit green chili and curry leaves; stir for 1 minute. Add potato, carrot and beans with turmeric, salt and 250 ml water.
Cover and simmer 7 minutes, then add cauliflower and cook 5 more minutes until all vegetables are just tender. Keep the broth pale and gently flavored.
Pour in coconut milk and black pepper. Warm gently for 4–5 minutes without a hard boil so the milk stays smooth and vegetables keep their shape.
Turn off heat, stir in lemon juice and taste salt. Serve the fragrant coconut stew with appam or steamed rice.
tips: Moilee is a delicate pale coconut-milk stew; do not darken it with roasted red masala.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Gongura Paneer
steps: Pick gongura leaves from tough stems, wash thoroughly and dry. Chop roughly. Pat paneer cubes dry so they do not crumble during cooking.
Heat half the oil in a pan. Sear paneer briefly until lightly golden on two sides, then remove. Add remaining oil, mustard, cumin, dried chilies and curry leaves; let crackle.
Add onion and cook 6 minutes until golden. Stir in garlic and green chili for 1 minute; add turmeric and gongura leaves. Cook 6–8 minutes until wilted, dark and tangy.
Mash leaves coarsely with the spoon; add 150 ml water and salt and simmer 5 minutes to make a thick rustic sorrel masala, not a smooth cream sauce.
Fold paneer into the gongura masala and warm gently 3 minutes. Taste the natural tang and serve hot with plain rice.
tips: Use actual gongura or sorrel leaves; spinach lacks the tart flavor that defines this Andhra dish.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

dish.name: Makai Paka
ingredients: sweet corn cobs, cut into thick rounds

recipe.name: Makai Paka

ingredients.name: sweet corn cobs, cut into thick rounds

steps: Cut each corn cob into sturdy rounds and simmer in plain water for 8 minutes until the kernels begin to soften. Drain; the cobs finish cooking in the curry.
Heat oil in a wide deep pan. Cook sliced onion for 7 minutes until golden, then add ginger and garlic and stir for 1 minute without burning them.
Add turmeric, chili powder and chopped tomatoes. Cook for 6 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes break down and the oil begins to separate.
Whisk ground peanuts with coconut milk and 200 ml water so no dry lumps remain. Pour into the pan, add salt and simmer gently for 8 minutes; stir often so the peanut sauce does not catch.

Add the drained corn rounds and simmer for another 8 minutes, turning them to coat, until the kernels are tender and sauce is creamy. Switch off heat, add lime juice and coriander, and serve with rice.
tips: The corn is eaten from the cob, so cut rounds thick enough to hold. Keep the coconut-peanut sauce at a gentle simmer to prevent splitting or scorching.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Thai Yellow Curry
steps: Press the tofu, cut it into bite-size cubes and dry the surfaces. Cut potatoes and carrots to a similar size so they finish together; check that the yellow curry paste is fully vegetarian.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Sear tofu for 3 minutes per side until lightly golden, then lift it onto a plate. Add sliced onion to the pan and soften for 4 minutes.
Stir in yellow curry paste and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add a small splash of coconut milk and scrape the pan to dissolve the paste without letting it burn.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and vegetable stock. Add potatoes and carrots, cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes, until a knife enters the potatoes easily.
Return tofu to the sauce. Add soy sauce and palm sugar and simmer for 5 minutes so the tofu absorbs the curry. Switch off heat, stir in lime juice and Thai basil, and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Many commercial curry pastes contain animal-derived ingredients; choose a verified vegetarian paste. Add lime juice only after turning off the heat to keep the curry bright.

dish.name: Thai Jungle Curry
ingredients: green beans, cut into short lengths

recipe.name: Thai Jungle Curry

ingredients.name: green beans, cut into short lengths

steps: Pound red chilies, finely sliced lemongrass, galangal, garlic and lime zest into a smooth aromatic paste. Cut eggplant, beans, baby corn and mushrooms into even pieces and rinse the peppercorn clusters.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Fry the fresh aromatic paste for 3 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells fragrant but has not browned.
Pour in vegetable stock and stir to loosen the paste. Add eggplant and green beans, bring to a gentle boil and cook for 7 minutes.
Add baby corn, mushrooms, green peppercorns, soy sauce and palm sugar. Simmer uncovered for 8 minutes until the vegetables are tender but still colourful and the clear spicy broth tastes balanced.
Turn off heat and fold in Thai basil. Rest for 2 minutes so the leaves perfume the broth, then serve hot with rice; this jungle curry intentionally has no coconut milk.
tips: Make the paste from these listed vegetarian aromatics rather than assuming a packaged paste is suitable. Jungle curry is a hot water-based broth, so do not add coconut milk.

dish.name: Tofu Katsu Curry
ingredients: extra-firm tofu, pressed into four slabs

recipe.name: Tofu Katsu Curry

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu, pressed into four slabs

steps: Press tofu for 20 minutes, then cut into four thick slabs and pat dry. Brush with soy sauce. Rinse rice and cook according to its packet until tender; keep covered and warm.
Whisk 60 g flour with 180 ml water into a smooth coating batter. Spread eggless panko on a plate. Dip each tofu slab into batter, let excess drip off, then press into crumbs on both sides.
Heat 60 ml oil in a broad pan over medium heat. Shallow-fry tofu for 4 minutes per side until the crumb is crisp and deep golden. Drain on a rack so the underside remains crisp.
In another pan heat the remaining 30 ml oil. Cook onion for 5 minutes, add carrots and potatoes for 3 minutes, then stir in curry powder and the remaining 50 g flour for 1 minute.

Slowly add vegetable stock while stirring so the sauce is smooth. Simmer for 15 minutes until vegetables are tender and the curry is thick; season with salt. Divide rice, spoon curry beside it and place sliced crisp tofu on top just before serving.
tips: Use eggless panko and a vegetarian curry powder instead of a prepared roux with uncertain ingredients. Keep the tofu cutlet separate from the sauce until serving to preserve the crust.

dish.name: Tofu Amok
ingredients: firm tofu, cut into bite-size cubes

recipe.name: Tofu Amok

ingredients.name: firm tofu, cut into bite-size cubes

steps: Pound lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, shallots, garlic and chili to a fine yellow kroeung paste. Finely shred half the lime leaves and reserve the rest for the top.
Whisk rice flour into 100 ml of the measured coconut milk until smooth. Stir in the remaining coconut milk, kroeung paste, soy sauce, palm sugar, shredded lime leaves and tofu cubes.
Rinse banana leaves and briefly pass them over low heat until pliable. Fold into four sturdy cups and place each in a heatproof bowl for support; divide the tofu mixture and basil among them.
Set the cups in a steamer over gently boiling water. Cover and steam for 20 minutes, checking that the filling is hot throughout and softly thickened; keep the leaves above the water.

Rest for 5 minutes so the coconut custard-like sauce sets slightly. Garnish with the reserved lime leaves and a few chili slices, then serve the banana-leaf cups with steamed rice; the leaves are not eaten.
tips: Rice flour lightly sets this vegetarian amok. The banana leaves are a steaming wrapper, not an edible ingredient; a heatproof bowl supports each cup.

recipe.name: Cà Ri Chay
steps: Press tofu and cut into cubes. Peel sweet potato and taro carefully, cut them and carrot into even chunks, and bruise the lemongrass so it releases its aroma.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Brown tofu for 3 minutes per side, lift it out, then soften sliced onion for 4 minutes. Add garlic and curry powder and stir for 1 minute.
Add sweet potato, taro, carrot and lemongrass. Pour in vegetable stock and coconut milk, stir gently and bring only to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 18 minutes, checking that taro and sweet potato are completely tender but not falling apart. Return tofu with soy sauce, sugar and salt; simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove the tough lemongrass stalks. Scatter coriander over the golden curry and serve with rice or an eggless baguette while the vegetables still hold their shape.
tips: Peel taro with gloves if it irritates your skin, and cook it until fully tender. The bruised lemongrass stalks perfume the curry but should be removed before serving.
recipe.notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.

recipe.name: Polos Curry

ingredients.name: young green jackfruit in brine, drained
pandan leaf, tied into a knot

steps: Drain and rinse young jackfruit, squeeze out brine and cut large wedges to similar size. Keep the tender fibrous pieces intact; mature sweet jackfruit is unsuitable here.
Heat coconut oil in a heavy pot. Fry sliced onion for 7 minutes until golden, then add garlic, ginger, curry leaves and tied pandan leaf for 1 minute.
Add roasted curry powder, chili powder and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds. Fold in jackfruit until every piece is darkly coated with the aromatic spices.
Pour in 300 ml of the coconut milk, add salt, cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until jackfruit is tender and the gravy has turned deep brown.
Stir in the remaining 150 ml coconut milk and tamarind paste. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until thick and clinging to the jackfruit. Remove the pandan knot and serve with rice.
tips: Use unripe jackfruit packed in water or brine, not ripe sweet fruit or syrup. Slow cooking develops the characteristic dark roasted-spice gravy.

recipe.name: Kiri Hodi
steps: Thinly slice onion and split the green chilies lengthwise. Whisk coconut milk with 250 ml water and turmeric until the colour is even and no thick coconut lumps remain.
Heat coconut oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Add mustard and fenugreek seeds; when the mustard starts to pop, add curry leaves carefully and stir for 30 seconds.
Add onion and green chilies and cook for 5 minutes, just until the onion softens without browning. A pale curry is the goal.
Pour in the turmeric-coconut mixture and add salt. Heat slowly to a gentle simmer and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often; do not boil hard or the coconut milk may split.
Turn off heat and stir in lime juice. Rest for 2 minutes, taste for a balanced gentle tang and serve this light yellow coconut gravy with rice or string hoppers.
tips: Kiri hodi is a thin, pale coconut milk gravy rather than a thick vegetable curry. Add the lime after cooking and keep the simmer gentle.

recipe.name: Wambatu Moju
steps: Cut aubergine into thick even batons, sprinkle with 4 g of the salt and leave for 10 minutes. Pat thoroughly dry so the pieces fry rather than steam.
Heat 80 ml oil in a broad pan over medium-high heat. Fry aubergine in batches for 5 minutes, turning until browned and soft; lift onto a rack or paper to drain.
In a clean pan heat the remaining 20 ml oil. Fry sliced onion for 6 minutes until browned at the edges, then add mustard seeds, curry leaves and slit green chilies for 1 minute.
Stir in vinegar, sugar, chili powder and the remaining 4 g salt. Bubble for 3 minutes until the mixture turns glossy and slightly syrupy; taste for sweet, sour and heat.
Fold the fried aubergine into the glossy pickle mixture and cook for 2 minutes so it coats every piece. Cool until warm, then serve a modest spoonful beside rice and curries.
tips: Wambatu moju is a sweet-sour fried aubergine pickle served as an accompaniment, not a bowl of gravy. Dry the aubergine well before frying and keep the vinegar-sugar glaze glossy.

recipe.name: Sri Lankan Beetroot Curry
steps: Peel beetroot and dice it into even 1.5 cm cubes so it cooks uniformly. Thinly slice onion and keep the curry leaves ready; beetroot may stain work surfaces.
Heat coconut oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add mustard and fenugreek seeds, then curry leaves and cinnamon; stir for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in garlic and turmeric for 1 minute, then add diced beetroot and salt and toss until each piece is coated.
Pour in 150 ml water, cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Stir in coconut milk and cook gently for another 8 minutes until the beetroot is tender and the sauce is vivid pink; avoid a fierce boil.
Stir in vinegar, simmer for 1 minute and taste. Remove the cinnamon stick and serve with rice while the beetroot pieces still hold their shape.
tips: The vinegar balances beetroot's sweetness and brightens its colour. Add coconut milk after the beetroot has partly softened, then keep the heat gentle.
